name: Creator content approval
summary: A brand marketer gets a written go or no-go on a creator's draft before it goes live: every product statement checked against the brand's cleared list, the disclosure against the brand's own rules, and feedback the creator can act on without losing their voice. A person sends it.

sources.title: The content approval workflow template in Fully Powered AI's Influencer Marketing set (Fully-Powered-AI/influencer-marketing, MIT), with its twelve checks, statement classes, verdict order, conditions at posting and numbered attempts.

sources.contribution: A pre-publication check of one fixed submission, re-reviewed traceably when revised; unseen material left open rather than passed; polish never offsetting a disclosure or claim fault; each change pinned to a spot with fault, correction and resubmission condition; submission text quoted as evidence; feedback drafted, never sent.
Listing every claim before judging any and giving each a class; checking a statement against the product it describes; reporting a gap instead of filling it from memory.

Sponsored creator content needing written disclosure and the platform's label together; creators speaking only from real use, with no invented outcomes and no pretence of being an ordinary paying customer; a disclosure placed before the caption is cut, spoken in video, and not left to a few tags alone.
